issues.description: Resolver no longer marks prepared/needs_more_preparation; state machine now relies on callers to call prepare_linked_requirements_more in the right order
issues.detail: The old resolver loop did `req.prepared = True; req.needs_more_preparation = False` after the more-prepare pass. Removing that block without changing the flags' semantics means those booleans are now only ever written inside prepare_linked_requirement(s)_more. Any caller that forgets to call prepare_linked_requirements_more (or calls it on a subset of requirement_set.requirements.values()) leaves requirements in an inconsistent half-prepared state. The data structure (per-requirement flags + an external multi-step preparer) is fighting the algorithm. The right shape is either: drop the flags entirely and make preparation idempotent, or own the staging in one place so callers can't get the order wrong.

issues.description: Three commands now repeat the same prepare-more incantation; obvious candidate for composition
issues.detail: download.py, install.py, and wheel.py each gained an identical `preparer.prepare_linked_requirements_more(requirement_set.requirements.values())` call at the top of their post-resolve section. That's the same line, copied three times, doing the same thing the resolver used to do for everyone. This is exactly the case where a small helper (or a `requirement_set.finalize(preparer)` method) replaces three drift-prone copies with one. Today they agree; in a year one of them will be subtly different and nobody will know which is right.

issues.description: set_dist/get_dist introduces a third source of truth for the distribution alongside metadata_directory and local_file_path
issues.detail: InstallRequirement already resolves get_dist() from `metadata_directory` or `local_file_path`. The new `_distribution` cache adds a third branch, checked first, with no invariant about how it relates to the other two. If later code populates metadata_directory after set_dist() was called with a metadata-only dist, get_dist() will keep returning the stale cached one. Data dominates here: the right structure is probably a single `dist: BaseDistribution | None` field that the preparer sets once, with the directory/wheel-file paths kept only as inputs to construction. The current shape preserves all three and hopes they stay consistent.

issues.description: download_info is being synthesized inside _fetch_metadata_only as a side effect, in the wrong layer
issues.detail: `prepare_linked_requirement` now reaches into the requirement and conditionally assigns `req.download_info = direct_url_from_link(req.link, req.source_dir)` when metadata-only fetching succeeds. The metadata fetch path is now responsible for two unrelated things: returning a dist, and patching download_info onto the requirement so unrelated commands (`pip lock`, `--report`) work. That's a filter that grew a side channel. Either compute download_info unconditionally where it's consumed, or have the metadata fetcher return a (dist, download_info) pair and let the caller assign. Hiding the assignment behind an `if req.download_info is None` makes the data flow harder to follow than it needs to be.

issues.description: set_dist is a one-line setter with no invariants; a plain attribute would be clearer
issues.detail: `set_dist` just assigns to `self._distribution`. There is no validation, no event, no laziness. In Python this is a getter/setter pair around a field — the kind of ceremony that exists in Java for binary-compatibility reasons and earns nothing here. Either give `_distribution` a real invariant (e.g. clear metadata_directory when it's set, or assert the link matches) or expose it as a plain `distribution` attribute and delete the method. Cleverness/ceremony should be load-bearing.

review.summary: The change moves a multi-step preparation pass out of the resolver and into each command, which is reasonable — the resolver shouldn't be downloading wheels — but the seams are rough. Three commands now repeat the same prepare-more line, and the per-requirement `prepared` / `needs_more_preparation` flags lost their one centralized writer, so correctness now depends on every caller doing the dance in the right order. The new `_distribution` cache on InstallRequirement adds a third source of truth alongside `metadata_directory` and `local_file_path` without an invariant tying them together; that's the data structure fighting the algorithm. The `download_info` patch inside `_fetch_metadata_only` is a side effect hidden in a metadata fetcher to make unrelated commands work — a filter with a side channel. Strip the get/set ceremony, lift the prepare-more call into one shared place, and pick one canonical field for the distribution.
